critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 2559 lines (was 2242 in iter8, +317 lines for priority/preempt code). Still well over the 700-line guideline. Suggest splitting preemption logic into /app/backend/preempt.py and priority CRUD into /app/backend/priority.py.

preempt_run() at server.py:2317 calls kill_checkout() which is itself an endpoint decorated with require_admin. Re-entering an endpoint from another endpoint is brittle (couples request lifecycle, dependency injection). Extract the core 'execute lmremove' logic into a private helper `_run_lmremove(srv, feature, user, host, display)` and have both kill_checkout and preempt_run call it.

_resolve_priority() runs an unbounded `db.priority_rules.find()` and walks 4 pattern matches per holder — O(rules × holders). For a 1000-rule, 500-checkout server this is 500k fnmatch calls per preempt/plan. Acceptable today but cache the rules list per request.

PriorityRule.priority allows 0–1000 (Field ge=0 le=1000) but releasable_holders is computed as 'strictly lower than requester' — a holder with prio 0 (no rule) is NOT releasable by a requester with prio 0. This is consistent with spec but worth documenting in the editor UI to avoid confusion (admin might set rule prio=0 thinking it's the floor).

SGE qstat/qmod paths are not validated (no shlex.quote in _sge_kill_job is fine since we do shlex.quote, but path is not checked to be absolute or to exist). On a real deployment a typo'd path will produce a generic timeout error that's hard to debug — add a /api/settings/sge/test endpoint.

/api/preempt/plan is NOT gated by require_admin (only /run is). Anyone authenticated can enumerate holder priorities + see who is checked out — minor info-leak. Consider gating with require_admin since the page itself is admin-only.
seed_reset (server.py:2407) has a dead `return {'ok': True}` on line 2425 after the prior return — unreachable code, lint warning.
